headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; low data-leakage and compliance risk due to limited Whisper I/O and Cognee’s allowlisted egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee can ingest documents and session memory, so if Whisper outputs transcribed text into a shared workspace or prompt chain, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. Whisper itself has no parsing or tool-use defenses, so the interaction risk comes from Cognee consuming its output. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are copied into Cognee prompts or memory without sanitization
IF Cognee treats imported text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor before Cognee ingestion
Review one sample transcript for prompt-like strings before enabling automation
Disable automatic import from Whisper outputs into Cognee memory
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all Whisper-derived text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Whisper is local-only with no network egress and no filesystem read/write, while Cognee has allowlisted egress and handles personal and finance data. The pair does not show a shared workspace or direct file bridge, so leakage is limited unless an operator manually moves sensitive transcripts into Cognee. Uncertainty stays low because no shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF an operator manually transfers sensitive audio transcripts from Whisper into Cognee
IF Cognee sends those imported contents to its allowlisted APIs
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs in a separate folder with restricted access
Do not paste transcripts containing personal or finance data into Cognee
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning on Whisper outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Whisper cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP, and Cognee’s profile does not claim filesystem write or git mutation. With no overlapping mutable resource exposed in the profiles, a write-write conflict is not plausible. The pair is therefore blocked by the documented capability set.
conditions: IF Cognee is later given filesystem or git write permissions outside this profile
mitigations: Keep Whisper and Cognee on separate workspaces
Avoid granting Cognee write access unless needed
requires-engineering: add lockfiles if shared mutable storage is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, so Whisper transcripts or summaries could become authoritative inputs if imported without verification. Whisper itself only produces speech-to-text output, which makes it a plausible upstream source for errors that Cognee may preserve or operationalize. The pairwise cascade exists in default text-ingestion workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are ingested into Cognee as facts
IF Cognee uses those transcripts to drive decisions or workflows without review
mitigations: Require human review before Cognee stores Whisper-derived facts
Mark Whisper output as untrusted in downstream prompts
Sample-check one transcript-to-memory path before rollout
requires-engineering: add verification gates for imported transcripts

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Whisper handles audio/speech that may contain regulated content. If audio transcripts include personal or financial information and are routed into Cognee’s allowlisted egress, retention or residency mismatches can arise. Only Cognee is cited for the sensitive data classes because Whisper’s profile does not specify compliance controls.
conditions: IF audio transcripts contain personal data or finance data
IF those transcripts are stored or transmitted by Cognee under a different retention policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated recordings from Cognee workflows
Document retention and deletion handling for transcript data
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
